Related Work and Positioning

MoCKA is positioned within the established research landscape of formal modeling, runtime governance, and semantic representation rather than as an introduction of a new mathematical theory. Existing formal methods, including transition systems and operational semantics, provide foundational mechanisms for describing system states, execution steps, and behavior constraints. These concepts have been extensively applied in software systems and verification-oriented domains.

Recent studies on runtime governance for agentic AI extend this perspective to autonomous systems by introducing policy enforcement, guardrails, runtime monitoring, and assurance mechanisms. Such approaches primarily focus on specifying acceptable behaviors, enforcing constraints, and evaluating compliance during execution. Similarly, semantic layer research has established methods for separating raw data representations from higher-level meanings used by users and systems.

MoCKA builds on these established concepts by applying them to the semantic operating layer of AI systems. Rather than proposing a new transition theory or governance framework, MoCKA introduces an architectural abstraction that represents governance-relevant semantic execution processes as structured transitions within a meaning lifecycle. The purpose of this abstraction is not to replace existing policy engines, guardrail mechanisms, or assurance frameworks, but to provide a semantic representation layer through which such mechanisms can observe and reason about AI execution contexts.

The proposed semantic transition abstraction therefore serves as an intermediate layer between existing runtime governance mechanisms and the evolving semantic states of AI systems. Existing runtime governance approaches determine how policies and controls are applied, while MoCKA focuses on how semantic execution contexts, evidence conditions, and meaning transformations can be represented in a traceable manner.

This positioning follows a complementary relationship with prior work. Transition systems and operational semantics provide the formal foundations; runtime governance and guardrail research provide enforcement and assurance mechanisms; semantic layer research provides meaning abstraction. MoCKA combines these established perspectives into an evidence-bound semantic execution model for AI systems without claiming to redefine the underlying theories.1. 第一候補：Claude（制度書記官・論文編集担当）
